key_facts: UPDATED Aug 14 (T+1d to Saturday Aug 15 final; SUBMITTED: Walsh 0.52->0.54, Douglass 0.42->0.38, Harris 0.03->0.06, Manuel 0.01 held, Huske 0.01->0; sum=0.99): (1) MEG HARRIS UPSETS WALSH IN 100m FREE (SwimSwam, NBC Sports, AP Aug 14): Australia's Meg Harris (defending 2025 World 50m free champion, 2024 Olympic silver medalist, 23.97 PB) upset Gretchen Walsh in Thu night's 100m free final (52.60 vs 52.78 from Lane 6), completely refuting CWG travel-fatigue concerns. Because Pan Pacs enforces a 2-per-country A-final limit, Harris is guaranteed a lane and wins ~4.5-5% if both Americans swim and ~15% if Douglass scratches (~0.06 total). (2) WALSH BLAZING MEET FORM (SwimSwam Aug 14): Despite fading slightly on the back 50 of Thu's 100m free final after opening in 24.97 (0.01s under WR pace) and setting a 52.57 PB in prelims, Walsh coasted to a 55.28 Championship Record in Fri morning's 100m fly prelims (nearly 2s ahead of the field!), confirming peak pure sprint speed alongside her 24.65 CR 50m fly and 23.60 swim in this Irvine pool on Aug 1. (3) DOUGLASS MIXED SIGNALS & SCRATCH RISK (SwimSwam, NBC Sports Aug 13-14): After scratching 100m free to focus on 100m breast, Douglass finished 4th off the podium in 1:05.81 (behind Siroky 1:05.32, Tang 1:05.46, Suzuki 1:05.65) and reportedly also scratched Fri's 50m breaststroke. While her 3-0 2026 H2H vs Walsh in 50m free finals, 23.59 former WR, Day 1 51.0 relay split, and lighter Fri morning schedule keep her a near coin-flip (~45% vs Walsh ~50%) if she swims, her demonstrated willingness to scratch sprint events to protect breaststroke keeps ~15-17% scratch risk alongside Saturday's 200m breaststroke. (4) HUSKE OFF FORM: Torri Huske missed the 100m free A-final (53.15 B-final win, behind Manuel 53.13 4th) and swam 57.72 in 100m fly prelims (~2s off PB); dropped from top-5, leaving Manuel (0.01) as primary US beneficiary if Douglass scratches.
